Commentary.Commentary: That brings us to the close of a one-sided affair. This time, South Africa were clinical for a change. After the drubbing they received in the Test series, they have come out with flying colours in the white-ball format. Sri Lanka, on the other hand, were not up to the mark. They need to put in an improved performance if they are to challenge an explosive South African side. Join us for the 2nd ODI from the same venue on 1st August at 1430 local (0900 GMT). Till then, cheers!

South Africa skipper, Faf du Plessis says that he is feeling much better after this win. Mentions that there was an opportunity for the seamers to get wickets in the first 15 overs and they had discussed just that. States that the breeze was a big challenge but feels that some past experience came to their rescue. Adds that the bowlers handled it well. Feels that they didn't play well in the Test series and admits that they have learnt some lessons. Opines that his batsmen took risks today and they paid off. Ends by saying that he is really looking forward to the upcoming games.

Sri Lanka skipper, Angelo Mathews says that he is disappointed with their performance. Feels that they have the ability to bounce back in the remaining four games. States that after the first 8 overs, the game had slipped out of their hands but Kusal Perera and Thisara Perera played really well to bring them back. Credits the South African bowlers for hitting the right channels. Ends by suggesting that a score above 250 would have been ideal on this track.

Man of the Match, Tabraiz Shamsi says that their fast bowlers were exceptional upfront. Adds that it made his task easier. Feels that the wind was a major factor and he had to make plans regarding where to bowl. States that this track didn't spin much. Appreciates the support from the team management and says that the dressing room atmosphere has been really good.

JP Duminy is being interviewed on the sidelines. He says that they had some conversations regarding their game plans. Adds that fortunately they worked today. Mentions that there were a few demons which were going on in his mind at the start of the innings. States that he is happy that his strokeplay came good today. Credits their bowlers for their performance. Feels there was something on the track in the first 10-15 overs and the seamers made use of it. Adds that they were looking to bowl the South African lengths and nick the guys out. Reckons that there was purchase for the spinners too. Ends by saying that they will be aiming to take the momentum forward.

Sri Lanka were over-reliant on their spinners to do the job but once their mystery was solved, they looked completely clueless. Akila Dananjaya picked three wickets but never looked threatening to run away with the game, apart from the fifth over he bowled. Probably a break in play after that gave the touring team time to regroup and rethink their strategies. The most disappointing performance was of Lakshan Sandakan who was not allowed to settle down, especially by Faf du Plessis. All in all, a pretty mediocre effort by the hosts in both the departments.

The chase began on a positive note for South Africa. Both Quinton de Kock and Hashim Amla looked positive and played their shots. However, the fifth over saw Akila Dananjaya removing Amla and Aiden Markram off consecutive balls. We all thought that will put the cat among the pigeons but the sensible heads of Faf du Plessis and de Kock managed to avoid any hiccups. They constructed an 86-run stand which steadied the nerves inside the dressing room and made the chase smooth. Despite losing both the set batsmen after that, South Africa kept pressing for runs and the experience of JP Duminy saw them through.

Earlier, some excellent pace bowling by Kagiso Rabada and Lungi Ngidi forced the hosts on the back foot right at the beginning. They bowled with venom and fire and dismissed Sri Lanka's top half inside the first Powerplay. Then, Kusal Perera and Thisara Perera combined for a counterattacking partnership of 92 runs to bring some sanity in the Lankan innings. Post that, Tabraiz Shamsi utilized the conditions to pick a 4-fer and helped the tourists in restricting Sri Lanka under 200.

Easily done. South Africa have turned the tables. Their fortunes have changed. They have passed the litmus test against spinners today and that mainly happened due to the aggressive approach they adopted against the Lankan tweakers. The Protea batsmen played the cross-batted shots to great effect and didn't allow the likes of Dananjaya and Sandakan to dominate proceedings.

FOUR! Duminy finishes it off in style! He also reaches his 26th ODI fifty, it has been a knock of substance from him. Shorter in length outside off, JP rocks back and cuts it through the point region to find the ropes. A clinical performance from the visitors and the customary handshakes take place. SOUTH AFRICA WIN BY 5 WICKETS, WITH 19 OVERS TO SPARE!
Spinning in, tucked through square leg for a run.
This one pitches outside off and skids through. Mulder tries to cut it but misses.

FOUR! Innovation at its best! On a shorter length outside off, Mulder gets into the position for reverse sweep and nails it past short third man. The ball races to the fence. South Africa are only a hit away from a victory.
Tossed up outside off, driven straight to the man at short extra cover.
Loopy delivery on a full length around off, swept away hard to deep square leg for a run.
Very full delivery around off, Mulder squeezes it out to the same region. Only 8 more needed for South Africa.
Pitched up ball around off, defended off the front foot to covers.
FOUR! Supreme timing! Too full and straight from Lakmal, Mulder holds his shape and flicks it beautifully past the short mid-wicket fielder. A boundary results.
Similar length ball outside off, blocked off the back foot towards cover-point.
Back of a length ball on middle, tucked towards short mid-wicket. Duminy wants a single but he is rightly sent back.
Short ball, pulled away to deep mid-wicket for a single. South Africa are doing it easily.
Suranga Lakmal returns.
This time JP gets under the ball nicely and sweeps it to deep square leg for a run.
Duminy gets into a bit of a tangle as he tries to sweep this one from outside off and gets hit on the pads.
Mulder uses his feet and taps this one through mid off for a single.
FOUR! Crisp! Brilliant way to get off the mark. Slow through the air on a fullish length outside off, Mulder leans ahead and drives it through extra cover to find the fence.
Tossed up outside off, swept away to deep square leg for a run.
Good running! Duminy stays back and plays this one with soft hands through the vacant mid-wicket region. Aggressive running between the wickets allows the batsmen to come back for the second.
Willem Mulder strides out to bat. 22 more needed. A slip in place for him.

OUT! Impact is umpire's call. Low full toss, tailing in from outside leg stump. Miller falls over a bit in an attempt to flick it and is beaten by the pace. He is hit flush on the front boot as the Sri Lankan players rise up in an appeal. The umpire obliges this time. Miller decides to signal for the 'T.' The replays roll in. The Snicko doesn't show any spike off the bat. The Hawk Eye now shows that the impact is umpire's call and it is hitting the stumps. The on-field call stays. A little too late for Sri Lanka though.
David Miller has been trapped in front of the wickets but he opts to take the DRS. Has he been hit outside the line? Let's find out.
The batsman has punched that ball through the off side.
Beaten! Back of a length ball, angling across David. He tries to punch it down the ground but is beaten on the inside.

In the air... but safe! Well-directed short ball, climbing on Duminy. He goes through with his pull shot but fails to control it. The fielder from square leg runs in but the ball falls well short of him. A run taken.

FOUR! The visitors are on a roll here. Length ball well outside off, Duminy reaches out for it and square drives it over backward point. The man in the deep dives to his left but ends up parrying it across the ropes.
Back of a length ball, Miller tries to punch it away but gets an inside edge beside the pitch on the leg side. The batsmen steal a run.
Suranga Lakmal is back on.

FOUR! The South Africans have used the slog sweep to great effect. Has been a high percentage shot for them. Slow through the air, allowing Duminy to get underneath it. He nails it through square leg to beat the diving fielder in the deep.
The arm ball from Jayasuriya, Duminy rocks back and chops it to the off side.
David comes forward and taps this one nicely to covers to rotate strike.
Miller leans ahead to the tossed up ball to play it past short leg. Thinks there is a run in it but has to send his partner back as the mid-wicket fielder is quick to attack the ball.
Spinning away from Duminy as he makes use of the depth of the crease to place it towards cover-point for a run.
A touch shorter in length, eased off the back foot to the cover region.
Wide! Drifting down the leg side, JP fails to connect with his sweep shot.
Jayasuriya returns.
Floated outside off, eased through covers for an easy run.
Helps this one around the corner to rotate strike.
The batsman has pushed it to the cover region. They have run through for a single.
FOUR! Sandakan overcompensates by dragging his length back. Duminy has ample time to rock back and slap it past backward point for a rocketing boundary.
SIX! Picking his spots to perfection is Duminy! Shutting the door for the Sri Lankans with his stroke play. Kneels to the fullish ball and hits it over long on to clear the fence.
FOUR! Shot! Loopy full ball outside off, Duminy lifts it over covers to pick up another boundary.
Miller places this one nicely past the man at 45 and takes a couple.

That almost went through the defenses! Turned square. On a shorter length well outside off, turning in sharply. Miller is hurried by it as he tries to keep it out but the ball hits his pads and rolls past his stumps.
Loopy delivery, kept out watchfully.
FOUR! Poor delivery and duly punished! Low full toss on the pads, Miller picks it up over mid-wicket to send the ball across the ropes.
Defended off the front foot by the batsman presenting the full face of the bat.

Almost deceived in the flight! Slow through the air, drifting in. JP uses his feet but gets it off the inner half of the bat towards short leg. The fielder fails to stop it cleanly. Duminy who was trying to get back in his crease sets off for a run and takes it safely in the end.
Outside off, chopped down in front of Mathews at first slip and then it looped over him. A single taken. A wicket and 6 from the over.
FOUR! Nicely done! Loopy delivery, Duminy kneels and sweeps it all along the ground through deep square leg to pick up a boundary.
Turning away from Duminy as he plays this with an angled bat to point.
The batsman shows the full face of the bat and defends the ball off the back foot.
Fullish ball, eased through mid off and Miller gets off the mark.
David Miller comes out to bat. South Africa need 65 runs from 161 balls.

OUT! Faf has thrown his wicket away! Needless to say the least. Du Plessis premeditates as he shuffles across a touch and tries to paddle scoop it over the keeper. However, Sandakan is cool as a cucumber. He smartly shortens his length, bowls it at a quicker pace and lands it wide outside off. Faf has to readjust but he does the mistake of flirting with it, attempting to run it down. An outside edge is induced and Mathews at first slip takes a good catch. The match is not over yet, folks. The two set batsmen are back in the hut and just like de Kock, du Plessis also misses out on his fifty. South Africa need to be careful.

Slower through the air, swept away hard past short leg. Kumara is ambling across to his right but realizes that the ball is coming at a fast pace. Dives at the last moment to cut it off. Two runs taken.
Defended off the front foot by the batsman presenting the full face of the bat.
SIX! Boom! Tossed up generously on off, Duminy decides to play against the spin and he does so with aplomb. He crouches and slog sweeps it over mid-wicket to send the ball all the way.

Edged but safe! Quicker through the air, pitching and spinning away. Duminy steps ahead to defend it but gets an outside edge that goes on the bounce towards Mathews at first slip. The key was that he played it with soft hands.
Once again Duminy stays leg side to the tossed up delivery and drives it to covers.
Full ball around the pads, Duminy clears his front leg and pushes it to mid on.
Floated outside off, turned with the spin to mid-wicket.
Too full this time, eased back to the bowler.
Wide! Spinning down the leg side, du Plessis tries to sweep it but misses.
A play and a miss! Floated well outside off, du Plessis goes for a booming drive through the line but the ball goes past the gap between his bat and pad.
Loopy full ball outside off, caressed to sweeper cover for a single.
Goes deep in the crease to the shorter one and answers it with a straight bat.
Just away from the reach of the extra cover fielder! Tossed up outside off, Duminy drives it uppishly as the fielder leaps to his right but the ball goes past him in a flash. Two runs taken.
Sandakan is back on.
Du Plessis allows the ball to turn into him and tucks it to mid-wicket. A wicket and 5 runs from the over.
Tossed up ball, defended solidly off the front foot.
JP Duminy is the new man in.

OUT! Quinton de Kock departs against the run of play! Dananjaya gets his third wicket, giving his side a sniff. He tosses this one up nicely outside off and it drifts away a touch as well. De Kock uses his feet and tries to go downtown but commits himself early into the shot. Ends up getting it off the outer half of the bat towards extra cover. Two fielders, Kusal Mendis and Suranga Lakmal converge towards the ball and it seems like there will be a collision. But they avoid it as Suranga takes the catch in the second attempt. The 86-run stand comes to an end. 77 needed from 176. Can Sri Lanka trigger a collapse now?
Drifting down the leg side, de Kock goes for the sweep but misses. The ball brushes the pads and goes towards the keeper.
Fullish ball on middle, eased past the non-striker to rotate strike.

FOUR! A gift and duly accepted! Short ball around off, spinning in. Faf du Plessis stands tall and pulls it over mid-wicket. The fielder in the deep has no chance to cut it off. Runs continue to flow for the Proteas.
Slow through the air on off, de Kock puts his head down and defends it calmly.
Good fielding! Short ball, ample time for Quinton to slap it towards backward point. The deep fielder moves to his right and gets low to stop it.

Floated outside off, de Kock once again goes inside out over covers. This time Kumara at sweeper cover comes into play as he runs to his left. However, he dives and almost makes a meal of it but recovers to keep the ball inside the ropes. It is checked upstairs and he is fine. Two runs taken.
Shorter in length, spinning away, cut to the backward point fielder who dives to his right to stop it.

SIX! Clean as a whistle! Jayasuriya comes around the wicket and bowls a tossed up ball outside off. De Kock makes some room, comes down the track and goes inside out over extra cover. The timing is spot on and the ball sails over the fence for the first maximum of the innings.
Tossed up ball in line of the stumps, kept out watchfully.
Loopy full ball on off, defended solidly off the front foot.
Smart bowling from Dananjaya. Sees de Kock using his feet and bowls it around his legs. Quinton does well to flick it to deep square leg for a run.
De Kock makes use of the depth of the crease to help this one to short fine leg.
Spinning into Faf who rocks back and milks it down to long on for a single.

Safe! The review goes down the drain for Sri Lanka! Tossed up ball around leg stump, spinning away. Faf du Plessis gets down on his knee and goes for a sweep but misses to get hit on the pads. Dickwella is convinced and goes up in a strong appeal. However, the umpire stays put. The keeper tells his skipper to go for the DRS to which he agrees. Time for the replays. The Snicko doesn't detect any edge. The Hawk Eye rolls in and the ball is pitching just outside leg. That puts the argument to bed.
Time for a review! Mathews has taken a review against Faf du Plessis regarding an LBW decision. Seems to have pitched outside leg. A review in desperation perhaps.
Full delivery on middle, whipped to short mid-wicket.
Akila Dananjaya returns.
Short ball, glided with the spin to the man at backward point.
Quicker and straighter one outside off, played off the outer half towards short third man.
Loopy ball outside off, tapped to covers.
Waits for the ball to turn into him and turns it around the corner to rotate strike.
The batsman flicks it away with a wristy shot.
Shorter in length, placed to the cover region for a single.
Shehan Jayasuriya is back on.
FOUR! Sandakan has no clue as to how to bowl to the South African skipper. He takes a couple of steps down the track and hits it over mid off to pick up back-to-back boundaries.
FOUR! Faf has been quite assured so far. Slow through the air, du Plessis comes down the track and lofts it down the ground to find the ropes once again.
Stump-to-stump line on a fullish length, eased back to the bowler.
The googly outside off, spinning away, left alone.
Full ball outside off, eased off the front foot to covers for a single.
FOUR! Well played! Tossed up delivery outside off, de Kock is quick to step out. He is not quite under the ball but manages to whip it through wide mid on to pick up another boundary.
In the zone outside off, punched off the back foot to covers.
Kumara bends his back again as de Kock goes for a heave but he ends up getting it off the inner half towards square leg. A run taken.
Continues to bowl a back of a length, de Kock works it towards wide mid on.
Similar delivery, pushed off the back foot back to the bowler.
Back of a length ball in line of the stumps, de Kock makes a bit of room and eases it to mid on.
Short ball aimed at the body, de Kock pulls it nicely to deep mid-wicket for a brace.
Uses his feet to this one but is not quite to the pitch of it and defends it eventually.

FOUR! Back-to-back boundaries! Short and outside off, asking for trouble. Du Plessis sits back and slaps it through backward point. The fielder in the deep runs to his left, dives, gets his hands to it but fails to stop the boundary. All too easy for the Proteas at the moment. That also brings up the 50-run stand between the duo.
FOUR! Sandakan is getting predictable now! Dishes out another wrong one which is spotted by Faf. He lifts it with the spin over extra cover to find the fence once again.
Googly on middle and off, worked away with the spin around the corner for a single.
Du Plessis is nimble on his feet as he knocks this one nonchalantly to long on to change strike.
Shorter in length, du Plessis camps back and blocks it right under his eyes.
Short of a length well outside off, crunched off the back foot to sweeper cover for a run. A good over from Kumara, only 2 from it.
Kumara is working up some good pace here. Bends his back and bowls a shortish ball on off. Du Plessis is hurried by the pace and defends it on the bounce to short leg.

Great work from Thisara! Back of a length ball, angling in, du Plessis times his punch nicely towards wide mid on. Perera runs to his right and dives full length to save a certain boundary for his side. That kind of commitment is needed from the players.
Shorter in length but this time the pace is gentle. Pulled away with ease to deep backward square leg for a single.
Fuller in length outside off, drilled to the fielder at extra cover.
Back of a length ball, skidding after pitching. De Kock is beaten by pace as the ball goes past his back foot defense to hit him on the thigh pad.

FOUR! The boundary spoils the over which would have been otherwise a brilliant one. Sandakan makes the mistake of bowling a half-volley outside off. Faf leans into it and drives it crisply past the diving cover fielder to find the ropes.
Sandakan is showing his tricks. Bowls the straighter one first up to du Plessis. He tries to defend it but gets beaten.
Good option to play the sweep and de Kock chooses the right delivery to play it. Kneels and sweeps the fuller one to deep square leg for a run.
That was risky! The wrong one, turns in more sharply. De Kock exposes all his stumps and somehow manages to chop it towards backward point. Had he missed, he was a goner.
Good stuff from Sandakan! He bowls a conventional leg spinner outside off and it stays a touch low. De Kock goes for a cut but he is late on it, thereby missing it.
Starts off with a wrong one, de Kock comes forward tentatively and gets an inside edge onto his pads.
Lakshan Sandakan to roll his arm over now. Can he break this promising stand?
Beaten! This was a poor shot and he rightly got foxed. Good length ball outside off, holding its line. Faf tries to force it through the line with zero footwork but misses it completely.

FOUR! He is growing in confidence! Sri Lanka need to keep a lid on the runs otherwise this match will run away from them. Full length ball outside off, du Plessis comes ahead a touch and strokes it through extra cover for an exquisite boundary.
Hangs back to the length ball and blocks it with authority.
Wide! Short ball outside off but it is too high as du Plessis bails out of his pull shot. The square leg umpire is quick to signal a wide due to the height.
Pitched up delivery, luring Faf to do something audacious. However, he is cool as a cucumber as he drives it to mid off.
Back of a length outside off, run down to third man for a single.

Howzat? The answer to that is not out. Back of a length ball on middle, leaving de Kock. He hops to block it but seems to have missed it. The ball deflects off something and carries to Dickwella behind. Kumara and the keeper appeal vociferously but the umpire shakes his head. Mathews thinks about a review but doesn't take it. Rightly so, as the replay shows that there was no bat involved.
Lahiru Kumara comes into the attack. He was brilliant in the Test series against the Windies. Can he deliver the goods here as well?
Shorter in length, answered with a straight bat.
Quicker in pace and skids off the deck. Du Plessis does well to adjust in his crease to keep it out.
The leg spinner this time, Faf is reading the variations well as he leans ahead to tap it to covers.
Fuller in length in line of the stumps, defended solidly off the front foot.
Spinning into du Plessis who turns it towards mid-wicket.
Slow through the air around off, pushed with the spin towards covers for a single.
Time for Powerplay 2! A maximum of four fielders are now allowed outside the 30-yard circle till the 40th over.
In the zone outside off, left alone.

FOUR! Stroked that with needle-like precision! Fullish ball outside off, du Plessis gets to the pitch of the ball and intentionally opens his bat face to find the gap. Drives it through cover-point. It is a teasing chase for the fielder who is after it from point but only comes second best.
Lakmal continues to bowl in the same channel, a more aggressive stroke from Faf as he slaps it but the ball goes straight to the cover fielder.
Short of a length outside off, du Plessis gets right behind it and taps it to extra cover.
Short leg comes in place.
This one lands on a length around off, takes off with some extra bounce and also seams in. Faf handles it quite well as he takes his bottom hand off the handle and dead-bats it.
Short of a length around off, glided to third man for an easy run.
FOUR! Crisp and confident! Loopy leg break outside off, Faf crouches in a jiffy and slog sweeps it over mid-wicket. Brilliant connection and another boundary results. 9 from the over.
Quicker in pace and the leg spinner this time, pushed off the back foot to the off side.

FOUR! Good execution! Slower through the air and on a fullish length on off, Faf kneels, gets his head right over the ball and with a nice extension of the arms sweeps it through square leg to pick up a boundary.
Turning in sharply from outside off, Faf makes good use of the depth of the crease and punches it to the cover region.
Fractionally shorter in length, de Kock rocks back and works it through mid-wicket to rotate strike.
Floated around off, tapped gently to short third man.

Nervy moment for du Plessis! He tries to chop away an inward shaping length ball but the shot selection is not good. There is no space to work with and he gets a bottom edge that just goes past the off stump.
On a length well outside off, run down to third man for an easy run.

There is something on this deck to keep the bowlers interested throughout. Got to make use of it. Pitches on a good length and it shoots off from there, landing de Kock in an uncomfortable situation. He tries to fend it away but gets hit on the gloves.
Well bowled! Attacking the ribs of Faf with a back of a length ball. He hops and tries to tuck it away but the ball goes off the thigh pads towards the left side of the keeper. A leg bye taken.

Lakmal switches to around the wicket and bowls a similar length ball. Quinton cuts it towards deep backward point. Sandakan stationed there fumbles but recovers in time to not give away an extra run. Only a single results.
FOUR! Played with authority! Back of a length ball, angling across the southpaw. De Kock holds his shape and flays it past the point region to find the fence.
Suranga Lakmal to bowl from the other end. A wide slip in place.

This one pitches and holds its line, skidding after pitching. Du Plessis plays for the non-existent turn and gets it off the outer half of the bat towards short third man. Good start after the break for Akila, only 2 from it.
De Kock uses his feet to this one, taking any spin out of the equation. Helped through mid on for a run.
Fuller in length on middle and leg, played with soft hands beside the pitch on the leg side.
A bit shorter in length, allows de Kock to read the googly off the pitch. He stays back and chops it to the cover region.
Slower through the air on middle and leg, eased down the ground to long on to rotate strike.
Bowls a straighter one on off and also hurries Faf. He gets it off the outer half of the bat towards the point region.

We are back after the break. They players and the umpires make their way out to the middle. It will all boil down to how the Protea batsmen tackle the Sri Lankan spinners. There is still a lot of fizz in this contest. Faf du Plessis will take the strike. Akila Dananjaya to continue his spell. Here we go...
...THE CHASE RESUMES...

Two wickets in the fifth over and South Africa will head into the break doubting themselves. They have a battle on their hands and it's not going to be easy for them against the Lankan spinners. The pair of Hashim Amla and Quinton de Kock started fluently though and it appeared that they will run away with the game. Akila Dananjaya's double-strike has pegged them back a bit and also given them a psychological blow as the Proteas will start to fret on the prospect of facing the spin-test yet again on a helping deck. 157 more needed. Game on. Do join us in a short while.
Tossed up ball and on off, defended off the front foot to end the over. The players are now heading back to the pavilion for a break.
Goes on the back foot and works it wide of mid-wicket for a run.
Loopy and on middle, helped to mid-wicket again.
Goes wide of the crease and serves it full on middle, de Kock eases it in the gap at mid-wicket for a run.
Flighted and full on off, defended off the front foot.

FOUR! Quinton has been quite fluent with his stroke play in this innings, especially through the cover region. Once again he is on the front foot to a full ball and delightfully strokes it through the gap on the off side. A boundary results. Good start to the over.
Shehan Jayasuriya to bowl the last over before the break.
Du Plessis has defended it by getting right behind the line of the delivery. Excellent over, just a run and a couple of wickets from it.
Easily negotiates the hat-trick ball. A flighted ball landing full on middle, Faf defends it watchfully.
Skipper Faf du Plessis to face the hat-trick ball.

OUT! Trapped in front! Back-to-back wickets for Akila Dananjaya. He has infused life in this game now. Another back of the hand delivery, a googly landing full around middle, Markram tries defending it but fails to read the variation. He is rapped on the pads, they appeal and the finger goes up immediately. He was a dead duck there. No need to take the DRS. That's hitting the leg stump, shows the replay. Like Amla, Markram also struggled in the Test series against spinners and is found wanting here too.
Aiden Markram is the new batsman.

OUT! Right through the gate! Akila tosses this one in the air, a googly and lands it around off. Amla stays back to work it around but misses the ball completely. It goes right through his defense to break the stumps. Once again Hashim displayed a very ordinary technique while playing a spinner. He was very poor in the Test series also and the same has happened once more.
Tossed up ball on off, de Kock bunts it down to mid on and scampers across to the other end.
A slider around off, de Kock gets forward and defends it from the inside half of his bat.

FOUR! Shot! Amla is looking in fine touch. A length ball outside off, Hashim doesn't get entirely forward, just times his stroke from the middle of the blade and places it past the left side of the cover fielder. Speeds through to the fence in no time.
This one is on the pads of the batsman, Quinton deflects it to fine leg for one.
Back of a length ball around off, Amla eases himself on the back foot and punches it sweetly through covers. Dananjaya chases it down in the deep and they take three runs.
Gets behind the line of the delivery and blocks it safely to the off side.
Excellent delivery. It's on a good length outside off, shaping back in slightly, Amla takes a long stride forward to cover the line and then shoulders arms.
A length ball on middle, Amla clips it off his pads but finds the square leg fielder.
Floated and full on off, de Kock presses forward in defense. Easy-peasy at the moment for South Africa.
FOUR! Beautiful shot! A little shimmy down the track by Quinton. He makes the length full enough for the drive and then crunches it through covers for a sublime boundary.
Fires this one flat and around leg, de Kock tries to flick but is beaten for pace. It goes off his pads to mid-wicket.
Spinning down leg, Amla works it in front of square leg and crosses. No real pressure at the moment applied by Sri Lanka.
FOUR! Well played! Too full this time, around middle and leg, Amla goes down on one knee and paddles it fine down the leg side for a boundary.
Flighted ball outside off, a bit on the shorter side, Amla goes back and helps it to mid-wicket.
Goes fuller this time, around middle and off, de Kock drives it confidently but finds the cover fielder.
Angling across the batsman, on a length around off, once again Quinton stays back in defense.
On a length around middle, defended off the back foot to the off side.
Defended off the front foot by the batsman presenting the full face of the bat.
Wide! Drifting down the leg side, Amla tries to flick but misses. Dickwella dives across to his left but fails to collect it cleanly. An extra run taken.

FOUR! Wrong line and length. It's too straight and angling down the leg side, Amla picks it off his pads and flicks it in front of square leg. The fielder inside the ring dives to his right but fails to stop it.
Begins with a back of a length ball on middle and off, de Kock defends it from the crease to the off side.

Suranga Lakmal to bowl from the other end with the second new ball. There's plenty of pace and bounce on this surface as shown by Rabada and Ngidi. Can the Test skipper get the same? Two slips in place...
Works it with the spin to the leg side, finds mid-wicket. Good start for the Proteas.
Excellent delivery. Full and flighted on off, Amla tries pushing it through the line but gets an inside edge past the stumps to fine leg. A brace taken.
Loopy and outside off, Amla lunges and defends it off the inner half of the bat to the leg side.
Well tossed up outside off but it's too full in length, de Kock stretches forward and drives it through covers for three runs.
A bit of spin from around off, de Kock is cramped for room and ends up hitting it back to the bowler.
Starts with a flighted full ball around leg, Amla nudges it in front of square leg and gets off the mark with a single. South Africa are away!
We are back for the chase! Hashim Amla and Quinton de Kock are the openers for the visitors. Whereas, Sri Lanka start with spin, Akila Dananjaya has the first new ball in hand. Here we go...
